verdict_text:
YES

The plan verifies the precondition first (160 tensors in each fine-tune, plus pairwise `equal` over the 112 non-MLP names via a full-match negative lookahead that excludes exactly the four MLP tensor names per layer), and together with the later copies of all 48 MLP tensors from each fine-tune this pins the name sets to be identical. Both task vectors are built against the unmodified base — `copy` ft→`.tv1`/`.tv2`, then `subtract_` the base into them (giving `ft - base`), then `scale_` by 0.4 — and only after both exist are they added back with `add_`, so the ordering hazard is avoided and the result is `base + 0.4*(ft1-base) + 0.4*(ft2-base)` in float32. The required checks are all present as `assert` transforms: the shared-tensor verification, 48 merged tensors (asserted for each of the two task-vector sets), and 160 tensors in the output after the scratch `.tv1`/`.tv2` tensors are deleted. Names are unchanged and the output path is exactly `out/T4/model.safetensors`.
